root_cause_evaluation.question: Which candidate root cause (missing independent time control vs physical surface/lattice/source/EOS inconsistency) has concrete source evidence in Family F4 DROP?

evidence_summary: Physical geometry is a simple rectangular prism tank [0, 0, 0] to [1.2, 0.4, 0.6] m with 5 planar DBC walls (bottom, left, right, front, back) and open top; no complex STL surfaces or irregular geometries.
Discrete particle lattice spacing dp=0.0025 m is perfectly commensurate with tank and fluid bounds.

Continuous mass matches discrete mass to machine precision: continuous pool=53.248 kg (3,407,872 particles * 1.5625e-5 kg = 53.248 kg); continuous drop=5.824 kg (372,736 particles * 1.5625e-5 kg = 5.824 kg); total continuous mass 59.072 kg.
Equation of state is uniform across resolutions: Tait EOS (gamma=7, rhop0=1000 kg/m^3, sound speed=24.8602 m/s).
Conclusion: No physical surface, lattice spacing, source mass, or EOS inconsistency exists between definition and discrete generation.
Zero independent temporal controls (neither halfstep, quarterstep, nor dense save) have ever been executed or registered for F4 fine DROP.

The completed spatial 3-resolution study (root_drop_three_dp_full_macro_review_006) failed the 5% continuum macro budget on fluid kinetic energy (0.08196 vs 0.05), vertical momentum (0.329525 vs 0.05), and drop kinetic energy (0.356088 vs 0.05).

The contact audit (root_drop_three_dp_contact_review_005) observed fine contact at 0.187003 s with whole event budget 0.0025542 s, and medium-fine bracket separation [0.001974 s, 0.003964 s] spans across the budget, leaving the bracket unresolved.
The fine native simulation incurred 13,986 excluded particles (0.218531 kg), which must remain classified as unknown numerical exclusions (not domain spill).

Crucially, the completed baseline solver log (Run.out) shows that 4,833 timesteps were clamped by DtMin starting at t=0.105067 s (impact onset), because the default CoefDtMin=0.05 enforced an acoustic floor.

If one only halved CFL (0.2 -> 0.1) without halving CoefDtMin (0.05 -> 0.025), the CFL-governed timestep would be artificially clamped by the unhalved CoefDtMin floor, creating unintended fixedDt floors.

Conclusion: Unresolved temporal shock dynamics and acoustic timestep clamping represent the primary physical mechanism behind the macro divergence; an exact true-halfstep execution clone with both CFL and CoefDtMin halved and zero fixedDt floors is the rigorous, bounded evidence-based path.
